This second application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.203/2021 registered at Police Station Sabhapur, District Satna, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376, 376(2)
(i)(n) of the Indian Penal Code read with Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: The applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 02.11.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No.49368 of 2022 granting liberty to revive the same after recording the statement of the prosecutrix.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail since 22.09.2022.
He submits that statements of prosecutrix and other material witnesses have been recorded.

He submits that from the statement of prosecutrix, it can be gathered that she was a consenting party and she went with the applicant with her own wish and physical relation got developed between them that too with her own desire.
He submits that out of the said relationship, the prosecutrix has delivered a child.
He submits that before arrest, the applicant and prosecutrix were used to reside like husband and wife, but now she is residing with her parents.

He submits that if the applicant releases on bail,
then he will keep the prosecutrix with him as his wife after attaining the age of 18 years by the prosecutrix.
Therefore, he prays that considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the applicant's custody period, he may be enlarged on bail.
On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that since the age of prosecutrix is below 18 years therefore, her consent is immaterial.
According to him, the bail application deserves to be dismissed.
Learned counsel for the respondent/objector has also supported the stand taken by learned Panel Lawyer and submitted that looking to the age of prosecutrix, her consent is immaterial.
According to him, looking to the nature of offence committed by the applicant, the offence has rightly been registered against him.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary and taking into account the statement of prosecutrix wherein she has admitted the fact that she and applicant entered into marriage, though her age is below 18 years, but looking to the fact that she delivered a child, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.

Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this application is allowed subject to condition that after release on bail, the applicant will neither try to contact the prosecutrix nor try to develop any physical relation with her, until she attains the age of 18 years.

However, as per undertaking given by learned counsel for the applicant, it is also directed that after attaining the age of 18 years by the prosecutrix,
if the applicant refuses to keep her with him as his wife, then the respondent/State will be at liberty to move an appropriate application for cancellation of bail.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.
It is further directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Certified copy as per rules.
